name: walk_trial_b
prompt:
Two images are attached. The first is a layout: 12 equal squares in a 4×3 grid on a flat magenta background. The second shows finished art from the same top-down 2D city game: roofs and cars, and on the right a square of the game's grass. Match that art's look: crisp, clean hand-painted game art in the muted cool greys of a modern European city, tidy and well kept. It must NOT look like a photograph: no blur, no photographic noise. It must not look rustic or old-town either: no stone flags, cobbles, pebbles or bricks.

Make one image with exactly the same 4×3 layout as the first image. Fill each square with the patch of city pavement — the ground people walk on beside a street — described for its row below. It is a ground texture the game repeats over large areas beside asphalt roads, and it must look good turned at any angle under a street running any way.

Shape comes first:
- Each square is filled edge to edge, right into all four corners, and stops exactly at its outline. Paint over the outline itself: the finished square has no border, frame, rim, bevel, outline, shadow or vignette, and its edges look the same as its middle.
- Draw nothing outside the squares. Outside them, keep the background fully transparent. No text, numbers, labels or grid lines anywhere.

Rules for every cell:
- Look straight down (orthographic). No perspective, no light falling off towards any edge.
- Each square is 9.2 × 9.2 m of ground. Keep everything true to size: a gum spot a couple of centimetres, a leaf a few centimetres.
- No direction and no regular pattern: never joints, slabs, tiles, a grid, rows, stripes, arcs, brush strokes or straight lines across the square; anything there lies at random, so the square looks the same turned any way.
- Even texture: the same tone and density all over the square, nothing that catches the eye, so it repeats without a visible pattern.
- Tidy and in good repair: no rubble, holes, potholes, big cracks, puddles or big stains.
- The four squares of a row are the same pavement: exactly the same colours, grain and style, so they can be joined without a visible seam. The first two of each row are clean; the last two are the same pavement a little more used.
- Nothing stands on the ground and nothing is painted on it: no markings, kerbs, drains, manholes or objects.

Row 1 — a city footway's asphalt: mid grey, clearly lighter and finer than a road's, a tight fine grain of tiny pale and dark specks, soft broad variations of tone. Cells 3 and 4 a little more used: soft lighter worn patches where people walk, a few small faint dark gum spots, a very few tiny fallen leaves.

Row 2 — light cool grey city concrete in one continuous surface, painted with soft broad mottling of lighter and darker greys, a fine grain, a few small dark gum spots. Cells 7 and 8 a little more used: soft grime patches, more small dark gum spots, a very few tiny fallen leaves, faint hairline cracks curving every way.

Row 3 — light grey terrazzo-like concrete: a smooth pale grey base densely set with small chips of white, grey, charcoal and a few soft blue-grey, 1 to 2 cm across, ground flat. Cells 11 and 12 a little more used: soft grime patches and a few small faint dark spots, still smooth.
